criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-10-02 has a mechanism naming an existing crates/ path and function (not "none"), owner Athena kept, and a measure ending in `status: <label>` where the label is a line `athena status` prints, or `status: not shown` plus the test name. Check with Grep on docs/spec.toml and the named path.
criteria.evidence: Grep of docs/spec.toml lines 1534-1540: mechanism names `improvement_cycle` in crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs and `improvement_cycle_line` in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. Both functions exist (introspection.rs fn improvement_cycle; status.rs:327). Owner is still "Athena". The measure names `cargo test -p athena-data cycle_tests` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test status_build_measurement` and ends with `status: not shown`, which is the form STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS' doc allows (status.rs:300-304).

criteria.criterion: A unit test for the cycle check passes with the mechanism: a record set with repair, supported finding, evaluated candidate and adoption decision reports shown; each set missing one stage reports that stage missing. Run `cargo test -p athena-data introspection` (or the crate holding the check). The test fails if the check is stubbed to always return shown or always missing.
criteria.evidence: All 4 cycle_tests passed: a_full_chain_is_shown, a_rejection_with_a_reason_is_a_decision, each_missing_stage_is_named, an_empty_record_set_is_not_shown. If the check always returned missing, a_full_chain_is_shown would fail (it asserts shown and the exact line). If it always returned shown, each_missing_stage_is_named and an_empty_record_set_is_not_shown would fail (they assert specific missing stages). Each of the four stages is removed in one case. The repair and candidate cases use `contains`, because removing those stages also removes the stages that depend on them.

findings.summary: The 'evaluated candidate' stage is always true for real proposals and checks no evaluation, so `athena status` can say the improvement cycle is shown when no candidate was evaluated.
findings.evidence: The stage counts as present when a proposal cites this job and at least one other job. proposals.rs:36 sets REPEAT_THRESHOLD = 3, and proposals.rs:310 writes no proposal for fewer than 3 distinct jobs, so every real proposal passes this filter. The cited sources are the failure cases that triggered the proposal, not cases the candidate was tested on. The requirement says the candidate is 'evaluated on representative cases' and the decision is 'evidence-based'. With this check, any accepted proposal citing a landed job that has a clean introspection makes the status line print `improvement cycle: shown`. Simpler, correct alternatives: report the evaluation stage as missing until an evaluation record exists (or add one, for example a baseline-versus-candidate result like method_experiment), or give the stage an honest name such as 'proposal on repeated cases' and keep the line from claiming 'evaluated'.

findings.summary: The new function was inserted between `build_measurement_line` and its doc comment, so the doc now sits on the wrong function.
findings.evidence: Lines 322-324 (the build_measurement_line doc) now sit directly above the new doc lines 325-326 and `pub fn improvement_cycle_line`. `build_measurement_line` at line 342 has no doc comment, and `improvement_cycle_line`'s rustdoc opens with text about build measurements.

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: The list names display.rs, commands.rs, records.rs, introspection.rs, spec.toml and CHANGELOG.md. The diff also changes athena-core/src/status.rs (where StatusView and the status builder actually live) and an athena-cli integration test file, and leaves commands.rs and records.rs unchanged. Both changes are the natural places for this work.

findings.summary: The chain does not link the finding to the proposal.
findings.evidence: `finding` is any recorded, unflagged introspection of the job. `candidate` is any proposal with a source for the same job. Neither the introspection id nor the failure class is matched against the proposal's sources or `failure_class`, so a finding about one weakness and a proposal about another can together count as one chain.

summary: The change adds `improvement_cycle` in athena-data and `improvement_cycle_line` in athena-core, makes `athena status` print an `improvement cycle:` line, fills in the OLY-10-02 mechanism and measure (`status: not shown` with the tests named), and adds tests. Every new test passed when I ran it, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. All six criteria are met. The verdict is still fail, because of one major soundness problem. The "evaluated candidate" stage only checks that a defaults proposal cites the job and at least one other job. Proposals are written only after 3 distinct jobs repeat a failure (`REPEAT_THRESHOLD = 3`, proposals.rs:36,310), so this check passes for every real proposal and does not test whether anything was evaluated. As a result, `athena status` can print `improvement cycle: shown` for OLY-10-02 when no candidate was ever evaluated on representative cases. Minor problems: (1) the new function was inserted between `build_measurement_line` and its doc comment, so that function lost its doc and the new one got a mixed comment; (2) two changed files (crates/athena-core/src/status.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/status_build_measurement.rs) are not on the deliverables list, while two listed files (commands.rs, records.rs) were not changed; (3) the chain does not check that the finding's failure class matches the proposal's.
